recentItems.title: Asiad: Gilas Men 3x3 leaving no room for error after perfect start
recentItems.description:
The Gilas Pilipinas Men are off to a strong start in the 2026 Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, but the Filipino hoopers are leaving no room for error as they move forward with their campaign.

After overcoming Mongolia and Sri Lanka on Monday, Gilas now turns its attention to Kazakhstan as its last assignment in the pool stage, and big man Luis Pablo is upbeat about their chances given their momentum.

“Yes, confident, pero at the same time, we don't underestimate any opponents,” said Pablo, who had six points and two rebounds against Sri Lanka.

Kazakhstan boasts one win after two games, having won against Sri Lanka before losing to Mongolia, and for Pablo, getting their third straight win would be a matter of who wants it more.

“Dito sa 3x3, any team can win,” he stressed. “Just like in 5-on-5, it's more on who wants it more and who's willing to put more effort to win.”

On the other hand, star scorer Nic Cabañero noted that Gilas’ defense will be key moving forward.

Despite leading the team in scoring through two games with 7.5 points and 5.5 rebounds, Cabañero said that limiting their opponents on defense will be their priority given how fast 3-on-3 basketball is played.

“Yung defense talaga magdadala sa amin ng panalo,” he said. “So we just need to stay composed.”

Gilas will return to action on Wednesday, September 23, to close out the pool stage against Kazakhstan.

recentItems.title: Fireworks light up sky over Nagoya as Asian Games open
recentItems.description:
Fireworks lit up the sky over Paloma Mizuho Stadium in Nagoya to celebrate the opening of the 20th Asian Games on Saturday (September 19).

The opening ceremony made a low-key start, with classical music and dance on a heart-shaped stage before the parade of nations which featured a delegation from reclusive North Korea.

The spectacle ramped up later though, with dancers in boiler suits marking Nagoya's manufacturing tradition and a fireworks display closing the night.

Emperor Naruhito’s visit to the ceremony was accompanied by a heavy security operation. Organisers had said up to 10,000 police would be deployed for the ceremony.

(Camera, Editing, Production and Writing: Irene Wang)

recentItems.title: Former sumo champ completes torch relay in Nagoya ahead of Asian Games opening
recentItems.description:
Former sumo champion Hakuho Sho completed the final leg of the torch relay in Nagoya on Friday (September 18), ahead of the opening of the Asian Games.

The Mongolian-born former professional sumo wrestler, with a record 45 championship titles, is widely regarded as one of the greatest sumo wrestlers in Japan's history.

As the final torchbearer, Hakuho brought the flame to central Nagoya, where he lit a small cauldron in front of a crowd gathered to mark the occasion. 

The 20th Asian Games will open on September 19 and run through October 4. 

(Camera, Editing, Production and Writing: Irene Wang)

recentItems.title: Alex Eala embraces 'opportunity' that comes with representing PH, Asia in tennis
recentItems.description:
SINGAPORE — When tennis star Alex Eala is told that she is an inspiration — particularly to Filipinos, and to athletes — she understands all too well what it means.

Not so long ago, the 21-year-old Eala was one of those young Filipinos who found herself looking up to an athlete who had reached the pinnacle of her sport. 

"Growing up, I really looked up to [former Chinese tennis star] Li Na," Eala said Friday in Singapore's NCO Club, where she was unveiled as the face of a hotel chain's official tennis platform. "That's because she's from Asia, and I [am] Asian.

"It has a huge power on people, when you see people where you come from, and they're being successful," she added. "There's a lot of inspiration in that."

"I feel it now, as an established player," Eala said.
